findings.description: Dereference of possibly-undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar throws — `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or empty, so every Google Meet booking without a destination calendar throws a TypeError and aborts event creation. Add optional chaining before `.integration`, matching the previous `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`.

Calendar references lose externalCalendarId for non-credential destinations — `createEvent` only sets `result.externalId` when passed a third argument, which only the `destination.credentialId` branch does, so references from the type-based and no-destination branches lose `externalCalendarId` and cannot be matched later. Fall back to the matching entry in `evt.destinationCalendar` for `result.externalId`.

Video credentialId is dropped when creating booking references — `createMeeting` returns a video `credentialId`, but this branch hardcodes `undefined`, and cancellation only calls `deleteMeeting` when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set, so Zoom/Webex/Daily meetings are never deleted. Use `result.credentialId` in the non-calendar branch too.

Collective team destination calendars dropped when organizer has none — `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op when both the organizer and event type have no destination calendar, discarding the co-hosts' calendars, which is the bug this PR targets. Build `evt.destinationCalendar` as `[...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]` instead of optional-chained `push`.

Fallback never matches, passing undefined calendarId to events.update — The fallback only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so its predicate can never match and `calendarId` reaches `calendar.events.update` as `undefined`, failing updates for references lacking `externalCalendarId`. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` as the fallback, as before.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:315-317`

updateLocation drops calendar credential and external IDs from references — `CalendarManager.updateEvent` returns no `externalId` or `credentialId`, so `updateLocation` persists references with both fields `undefined` and later updates and cancellations cannot resolve the right calendar. Fall back to the matching entry in `booking.references` when `result` lacks them, as the previous code took these from `evt.destinationCalendar`.

Recurring calendar deletion sweep repeats for each booking reference — The sweep is nested in the new `bookingCalendarReference` loop but does not depend on `reference`, so a booking with N references issues N× the identical `calendar.deleteEvent` calls and duplicates in `apiDeletes`. Run the sweep only once, not per reference.

Team admins rejected because admin/owner checks are combined with && — Since `isTeamAdmin` already matches ADMIN or OWNER, the `&&` with `isTeamOwner` rejects admins who are not owners. Use `||`, or just `isTeamAdmin`, so team admins can add guests.

addGuests allows adding guests to cancelled or rejected bookings — Without a `booking.status` check, a cancelled or rejected booking gets new attendees and a CONFIRMED invite, resurrecting it in every calendar. Reject `CANCELLED` and `REJECTED` bookings before adding guests.

Guest email blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive — Because `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased but `guest` is not, changing the casing bypasses `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`. Lowercase both sides as in checkIfBookerEmailIsBlocked.ts, and normalize the attendee duplicate comparison too.

Attendees can append guests to someone else's booking — The `isAttendee` clause lets any attendee append arbitrary addresses to someone else's booking, sending invites and branded emails as the organizer. Restrict this mutation to `isOrganizer` or `isTeamAdminOrOwner`, or require organizer confirmation.

Add guests action bypasses disableGuests and seatsPerTimeSlot — Guests can be added to event types with `disableGuests` or `seatsPerTimeSlot`, bypassing those constraints and creating seatless `Attendee` rows. Guard both the `add_members` action and `addGuestsHandler` against both fields.

Non-atomic duplicate attendee check allows concurrent duplicate guests — The `booking.attendees.some` check and `createMany` are not atomic, so concurrent calls insert duplicate attendee rows. Run the check and insert in a transaction with a unique index on (bookingId, email), or lock per booking.

sendAddGuestsEmails receives raw guests instead of filtered uniqueGuests — Passing raw `guests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails` sends a second full confirmation to addresses already filtered out of `uniqueGuests`. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead.

Deduplicate guest emails inside the addGuests request payload — `uniqueGuests` never dedupes against itself, so repeated emails in one payload are inserted twice by `createMany` and get two invites. Dedupe `guests` through a `Set` before filtering.

App metadata lookup uses public slug instead of metadata key, causing 404 — `appStoreMetadata` is keyed by directory name while `app.slug` holds the public slug, so most apps resolve to `undefined` and return 404, breaking credential sync. Look up the entry by `dirName` (selected alongside `slug`) instead.

Refresh response without refresh_token overwrites stored token with placeholder — When the response omits `refresh_token`, this writes the literal `"refresh_token"` over the stored credential; for Office 365 (optional `refresh_token` in `refreshTokenResponseSchema`) it is persisted and permanently breaks later refreshes with `invalid_grant`. Keep the caller's existing refresh token instead of injecting a placeholder.

Refresh token wrapper stored as credential key breaks Google auth — `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the `SafeParseSuccess` wrapper, so storing it as the credential key makes `googleCredentialSchema.parse` fail in `googleAuth` on the next read and breaks Google Calendar after the first refresh. Persist `key.data` instead.

Sync path returns raw fetch Response instead of parsed token JSON — Callers like `googlecalendar`, `hubspot`, `zoho-bigin`, and `zohocrm` expect provider-native token shapes, so returning the raw `Response` makes them no-op, crash, or overwrite the stored credential in shared mode. Return `await response.json()` or normalize each caller.

refreshOAuthTokens receives credentialId instead of owning user id — `refreshOAuthTokens` is passed `credentialId` as its `userId`, so the sync endpoint fetches another user's tokens or none and persists them onto this credential. Pass the credential's `userId` instead.

Connection is built with stale access token after refresh — The `jsforce.Connection` is built right after refresh from the pre-refresh `credentialKey.access_token`, so an expired token still fails despite the fresh one being saved. Use `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` and the refreshed `instance_url` when constructing it.

Salesforce token refresh validates via statusText instead of response.ok — `statusText` is empty for HTTP/2 and for servers omitting a reason phrase, so a valid 200 response throws `HttpError` and every Salesforce calendar operation fails. Check `response.ok` and read the body for the error message.

Salesforce client creation always refreshes token regardless of expiry — `getClient` runs on every constructor call, so each booking and calendar fetch now triggers a Salesforce token round trip and a `prisma.credential.update` write. Only refresh when the stored token is actually expired.

Webhook secret compared with timing-unsafe string inequality — The strict inequality short-circuits on the first differing byte and leaks the secret prefix through timing on this unauthenticated endpoint. Compare with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` over equal-length buffers after confirming the header is a string.

Race condition can create duplicate app credentials — Without a transaction or a unique constraint on userId+appId, concurrent webhook deliveries both `create`, leaving duplicate credentials where `findFirst` returns an arbitrary stale row. Add a unique constraint and `upsert`, or wrap the check-and-write in a serializable transaction.

Do not increment retryCount when SMS sending is locked — `twilio.scheduleSMS` returns `undefined` when sending is locked, and `checkSMSRateLimit` sets that state automatically once the monthly limit is hit, so a temporarily locked user permanently loses all reminders after two cron runs. Only increment `retryCount` for genuine provider errors and skip when sending is locked.

SMS cleanup deletes EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders with retryCount > 1 — Without a `method` filter this SMS cron hard-deletes EMAIL and WHATSAPP `WorkflowReminder` rows whose `retryCount` exceeds 1. Scope the branch with `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` so only SMS reminders can be deleted, matching `scheduleWhatsappReminders.ts`.

Unguarded retryCount update in catch can abort reminder batch — If `prisma.workflowReminder.update` throws — say P2025 after the new `deleteMany` removed the row — the exception escapes the loop and skips every remaining reminder in the batch. Wrap the increment in its own try/catch or use `updateMany` so error handling cannot abort the batch.

Missing index on WorkflowReminder retryCount causes cron full scan — No index supports `retryCount`, per `schema.prisma`, so this `deleteMany` full-scans the multi-million-row `WorkflowReminder` table on every cron run. Add an index on `retryCount` or on `(method, retryCount)` in the migration.

Backup-code login bypasses password when TOTP code is supplied — A request with a valid backup code and any `totpCode` logs in without the password, so a copied backup code alone unlocks the account. Verify the password unconditionally in the backup-code path before accepting the code.

Backup code comparison is case-sensitive, rejecting uppercase codes — Codes are stored as lowercase hex but `indexOf` matches them case-sensitively, so a user typing uppercase codes gets `IncorrectBackupCode` and is locked out. Normalize both sides with `toLowerCase()` before comparing, and apply the same fix in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`.

Backup code redemption has a non-atomic read-modify-write — Two parallel requests with the same code both pass `indexOf` and both authenticate, and concurrent redemptions of different codes can overwrite each other, breaking the single-use guarantee. Consume the code with an atomic conditional update, such as `prisma.user.updateMany` guarded by the original `backupCodes`, and fail when the count is not one.

resetState not called when modal is dismissed via X, Escape or backdrop — Closing the dialog with X, Escape, or the backdrop leaves `step` at `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes`, so reopening shows the previous codes with no Cancel button to escape. Call `resetState` from the dialog's open/close handler, not only from the footer buttons.

2FA backup-code dismissal skips onEnable and leaves stale step — Once the enable request succeeds, dismissing the dialog never calls `onEnable`, so the security page still shows 2FA as disabled, and the stale backup-codes step reappears on reopen. Call `onEnable` and `resetState` on dialog dismissal after the request succeeds.

Deleted caching tests leave authorization/filter caching unverified — Without these tests, nothing asserts that `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` cache their results, so a regression that recomputes conditions on every call would pass the suite. Restore the two caching assertions using the new `Prisma.sql` expectations.

Raw HTML cook method bypasses sanitization for imported feed content — Because `cook_methods[:raw_html]` returns `raw` untouched, third-party HTML from `TopicEmbed.import` reaches the page unsanitized, letting `<script>` or `onerror` run in the Discourse origin. Sanitize the imported HTML with a tag, attribute, and scheme allowlist before storing it, rather than relying on the cook bypass.

Invalid `end if` in embed/best template causes SyntaxError — ERB compiles the whole view into one method, so `<%- end if %>` leaves it unbalanced and every render of `embed/best` raises a SyntaxError, including the empty-topic branch. Change it to `<%- end %>`.

nil feed content raises NoMethodError and aborts the poll — `i.content` is nil for items that only carry `<description>`, so `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError, aborts the `each` loop, and skips all remaining items with no retry. Read the body defensively from `i.content` or `i.description` and skip blank items.

add_column with default rewrites posts and blocks access on PostgreSQL — On PostgreSQL before 11 the default and NOT NULL force a full table rewrite under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, blocking all reads and writes to posts for the whole migration. Add `cook_method` nullable without a default, backfill in batches, then set the default and NOT NULL afterward.

Unguarded embed.post causes NoMethodError for orphaned topic embeds — A `topic_embeds` row outlives hard-deleted posts, so `PostRevisor.new(nil)` raises NoMethodError, aborting the `rss.items` loop in `Jobs::PollFeed` and leaving all later items unimported. Return early when `post.blank?` or delete the stale embed.

Feed poll runs inline for every distinct embed URL retrieval — `perform_retrieve` pays the full O(feed items) poll inline for every distinct `embed_url`, since the `retrieved:` throttle is per URL and `feed_key` is unused. Enqueue the poll as its own throttled job instead of running it inline per request.

Remote embed fetch lacks timeouts and size cap — A slow remote response blocks the worker indefinitely and an oversized body is loaded entirely into memory by `open(url).read`, reachable from the embed endpoint. Pass explicit `open_timeout` and `read_timeout` and cap the bytes read.

Migration dereferences nil PG rows for missing site settings — The migration aborts with `NoMethodError` whenever no matching row exists, which is the normal case for `embed_category` and blocks the upgrade. Guard both lookups with a `cmd_tuples` check like the block below already does.

SQL injection in embeddable_hosts migration via string interpolation — A stored host containing an apostrophe crashes the migration, and other SQL fragments are executed with migration privileges. Pass the value through `connection.quote` instead of interpolating it.

Migrated embeddable hosts keep URL scheme and never match — Values stored with `http://` bypass the model's `before_validation` normalization, so `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` never matches the scheme-free `uri.host` and embedding silently stops working. Strip the scheme and path before inserting, or route the insert through the model.

Missing embeddable host causes NoMethodError in update and destroy — A stale or crafted id raises `NoMethodError` and returns a 500 instead of a JSON error. Raise `Discourse::NotFound` unless the `EmbeddableHost` lookup returns a record before calling `save_host` or `destroy`.

before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil — A request that omits `host` raises `NoMethodError` in this callback and 500s before `validates_format_of` can report the field error. Skip the `sub!` calls when `host` is blank so validation handles it.

Duplicate OptimizedImage.downsize breaks 5-argument emoji call — The 4-argument `downsize` at line 149 shadows the 5-argument version, so `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` calling it with 5 arguments will raise `ArgumentError` and custom emoji stop being downsized. Remove the dead definition and convert the emoji caller to a single `"100x100"` argument.

Animated GIF form uploads are downscaled to a static frame — `allow_animation` never matches because `downsize_instructions` tests the extensionless tempfile path, so animated GIFs collapse to a static frame. Pass the original `filename` into the downsize call as `app/models/upload.rb` already does.

Upload size validation ignores admin-configured max size settings — Hardcoding 10MB drops the `max_<type>_size_kb` lookup, so client-side validation no longer honors admin limits and `utilities-test.js.es6:52` can no longer trigger `file_too_large`. Keep the `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` lookup.

Oversized images not rejected after failed downsize attempts — A file still oversized after 5 passes is only rejected later by `Validators::UploadValidator#maximum_image_file_size`, wasting up to 5 conversions before the user sees an error. Derive the scale from `tempfile.size / SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` and abort explicitly if it stays too large.

Oversized uploads run up to five ImageMagick passes — Each oversized upload runs up to five full ImageMagick cycles plus `ImageOptim` in `convert_with` (app/models/optimized_image.rb), multiplying CPU cost for large files. Resize once with a factor from the size ratio rather than iterating relative 80% steps.

Public group members endpoint truncates default member list — Groups with more than 50 members silently hide the rest because the public members template has no pagination and never sends `limit` or `offset`. Page the endpoint from the client or return the full list for visible groups.

add_members fails when adding existing group members — Adding an existing member or repeating a name raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` and the request 500s, which is common since the admin UI never filters existing members. Skip usernames already in the group before calling `group.add`.

remove_member raises RecordNotFound when user is not a group member — A stale list, concurrent removal, or double submit turns this into `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` instead of a no-op. Look the user up through `group.users.where(id: user_id).first` and delete only when found, still returning success.

totalPages overcounts pages when user_count is a multiple of limit — An exact multiple of `limit` reports a page that does not exist, so `showingLast` stays false and the next arrow loads an empty list. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` so the last-page guard matches the real page count.

group.users.delete bypasses primary group cleanup and counter cache — Deleting the join row directly bypasses `destroy_deletions`, so a removed user keeps `primary_group_id` set and `user_count` drifts. Route removal through `usernames=` or explicitly clear `primary_group_id` for the removed user.

`SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` raises NoMethodError when default_locale is nil — A nil `default_locale` raises `NoMethodError` inside `I18n.fallbacks[]` during translation lookups, since `compact` runs after `to_sym`. Build the array first and guard before calling `to_sym`.

Translation cache is not invalidated when default_locale changes — Users keep seeing text from the previous site locale after an admin changes `default_locale`, since the `translate_accelerator.rb` LRU key omits the resolved fallback chain. Include the current `SiteSetting.default_locale` in the cache key or clear `@cache` when it changes.

Fallback chain loaded only on controller path, not in jobs or rake tasks — In Sidekiq threads and rake tasks the `SiteSetting.default_locale`/`:en` fallbacks are looked up against locale files that were never loaded, so missing keys render "translation missing" instead of fallback text. Call `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` wherever the locale is changed for a context.

Rejected device stays cached, bypassing the device limit — A device that was just rejected gets cached by `localCache.SetDefault` before the store call, so its next request returns early and the limit is bypassed. Move that cache write after the store call succeeds.

Non-atomic device limit check allows exceeding the limit — Concurrent requests all see `count < deviceLimit` before any write lands, so bursts can exceed the limit by any amount. Make the check and insert atomic with a transaction, lock, or unique constraint.

Anonymous auth blocks on TagDevice DB round-trips — Every uncached anonymous request now pays a `SELECT COUNT(*)` plus a write against `anon_device` on the auth path, and blocked devices still do a COUNT and failing UPDATE each time. Move `TagDevice` back off the request path.

Retry closure reassigns captured args, duplicating query on retry — `WithDbSession` retries the callback on lock errors, and reassigning the captured variable prepends the query again, sending it twice. Build the args slice locally inside the callback.

Missing cache re-check causes duplicate manifest parses — Goroutines that raced past the `RLock` check repeat the whole manifest parse while holding `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()`, serializing concurrent requests behind a blocking parse on cold starts and whenever the parse fails. Re-check `entryPointAssetsCache` under the write lock and return early if it was populated by the goroutine that won the race.

Async legacy writes use request context canceled after response — The legacy `Create`/`Update`/`Delete`/`DeleteCollection` run under the request context, which Go cancels as soon as `ServeHTTP` returns, so each aborts with `context.Canceled` right after the response and the dual write never happens. Detach the goroutine with `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` while keeping request values.

Async legacy update reuses raw objInfo instead of persisted result — `Legacy.Update` re-invokes `objInfo.UpdatedObject` on the legacy store's own old object, so the legacy copy can diverge from unified storage. Wrap the persisted `res` in `updateWrapper` as modes 1 and 2 do and pass that to `d.Legacy.Update`.

Async legacy writes in mode 3 can be applied out of order per object — Fire-and-forget goroutines drop the ordering guarantee: a create-then-delete, as in `playlist_test.go:506-576`, can reach legacy reversed and leave the row orphaned. Serialize the async legacy writes per object with a single worker queue keyed by kind+name.

Legacy DeleteCollection records to storage histogram instead of legacy — Legacy latency lands in the storage histogram and legacy failures stay invisible in `grafana_dual_writer_legacy_duration_seconds`. Call `d.recordLegacyDuration`, as the other legacy calls do.

Delete storage duration metric uses object name as kind label — `recordStorageDuration` gets the object `name` in the `kind` label, so every deleted object adds a new `grafana_dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds` series (unbounded growth, unusable filtering). Pass `options.Kind` instead.

Create error path records legacy duration instead of storage duration — The storage failure goes to the legacy histogram, so `grafana_dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds` never shows `is_error=true` and legacy gets a false spike. Record it with `d.recordStorageDuration` instead.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:125-129`

Concurrent cache misses can build duplicate indexes for same key — `getOrCreateIndex` now checks `GetIndex` outside any per-key lock, so two concurrent misses build separate indexes in the same directory and one caller keeps writing to an index already replaced in `b.cache`, making those documents unsearchable. Add per-key deduplication or an in-flight map so only one build per `NamespacedResource` runs at a time.

Logging TotalDocs races with watcher cache writes — The watch goroutine started just above can write the same cache under `cacheMu` while this call reads it, causing a concurrent map read/write panic. Synchronize `TotalDocs` with the cache writer or run it before the watcher starts.

Eager Init leaks watcher on unmanaged in-process servers — In-process servers from `restoptions.go` and `legacy_storage.go` have no `Stop` call site, so each construction starts a broadcaster goroutine and appends a subscriber to `dashboardSqlAccess.subscribers` that is never removed. Keep initialization lazy for servers that are not lifecycle-managed, or trigger shutdown for those construction paths.

Init failure leaks watcher and event-pump goroutines — The discarded instance never gets `Stop`, so the broadcaster and the `backend.WatchWriteEvents` subscription from `initWatcher`, plus the search event pump, keep running against the database forever. Call `s.cancel()` and close the started watchers on the error path before returning.

Silence menu item shown in list view but cannot open drawer — In the list view the visible "Silence notifications" item does nothing, because `RuleActionsButtons.V2` only mounts `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` when a ruler rule is present and the list view passes no `rulerRule`. Gate the silence item on a ruler rule being present, or make the drawer work from the promRule/uid.

Federated Mimir rule groups are treated as editable — Federated Mimir rule groups are read-only server-side, yet every view going through `useAlertRuleAbility` now reports Update/Delete/Pause as supported and shows actions that fail. Thread the federation check through from `rule.group` or pass a flag into this hook.

New abstract getShortcut() breaks binary compatibility for custom grants — Any externally deployed custom `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` compiled against the previous SPI throws `AbstractMethodError` when `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` calls `getShortcut()`, so the server fails to start after upgrade. Give `getShortcut()` a default implementation, such as deriving it from `getId()` or returning the UNKNOWN `na` value.

Duplicate null check on grantType means rawTokenId is never validated — Because `grantType` is checked twice, a null `rawTokenId` is silently encoded as the literal "null" suffix instead of failing fast. Change the second check to `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`.

Grant shortcut length is not validated before token ID encoding — A grant factory returning a 3-character shortcut mints access tokens whose IDs always throw `IllegalArgumentException` in `getTokenContextFromTokenId`, which requires exactly 6 characters. Validate that the shortcut is exactly 2 characters in `encodeTokenId`, or make the decoder length-agnostic.
client_credentials tokens encoded with UNKNOWN grant type — Set it before `generateAccessToken()` so the new `cc` shortcut is emitted.

isAccessTokenId checks wrong grant substring and inverts the comparison — `substring(3, 5)` reads the token type's second character plus the grant's first character, so the grant shortcut is never validated. Use `substring(4, 6)`, otherwise every valid encoded token ID is rejected once the inverted comparison is fixed.

getSubGroupsCount returns null for deleted group, violating SPI contract — Consumers that unbox or aggregate the count now throw an NPE on a concurrently deleted group, moving the crash to a harder-to-diagnose layer. Return a non-null value such as `0L`, or re-resolve through the delegate and signal a controlled failure.

Reader thread can hang test JVM if group deletion throws — Any exception from `group(groupUuid).remove()` leaves the non-daemon reader thread spinning forever and hangs the whole test JVM. Wrap the deletion loop in `try/finally` that always sets `deletedAll`, and preferably make the thread a daemon.

Reader thread not joined before asserting caught exceptions — A failure from an in-flight `groups()` request is appended after the assertion already passed, so the regression this test targets can be missed. Join the reader thread before checking `caughtExceptions`.

Reader thread busy-spins on full group listings and unbounded errors — The unbounded `caughtExceptions` list and full-hierarchy reads on every iteration can saturate CPU or fail with OOM instead of reporting the assertion. Add a small delay and record only the first failure.

Choice-format normalization hides embedded markup from sanitizer — Dropping the whole `{N,choice,...}` segment in `normalizeValue` lets embedded markup like `` bypass the sanitizer for `error-invalid-multivalued-size` and `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*`. Neutralize only the `<` characters in the choice pattern so choice literals are still sanitized.

Lithuanian account messages totpStep1 replaced with Italian text — Lithuanian users of the account and login TOTP setup pages now see Italian instructions. Restore the Lithuanian translation in `totpStep1`; the same wrong-language string is also in `messages_lt.properties` under the login theme.

error-invalid-multivalued-size uses MessageFormat syntax breaking i18next — i18next only interpolates `{{ }}`, so `error-invalid-multivalued-size` displays raw `{0}` and `{2,choice,...}` text in the admin UI and conflicts with existing translations. Keep `{{0}}`/`{{2}}` here and in the account `messages_en.properties`; the `choice` form belongs only in server-side theme bundles.

**Also found in:**
- `js/apps/account-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v3/account/messages/messages_en.properties:188-188`

getClientsWithPermission returns bogus entry instead of client ids — The set ends up with the all-clients resource's literal name instead of client ids, so AvailableRoleMappingResource throws a NullPointerException on `realm.getClientById(cid)`. Iterate real clients and add `client.getId()` when `hasPermission` passes.

Existing realms miss upgrade for new CLIENTS admin resource type — Realms with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 already enabled never get the new scopes or the CLIENTS resource type, and `getOrCreateResource` fails with ModelException("No scopes found."). Add reconciliation for existing admin-permissions resource servers when the schema grows.

ClientPermissionsV2 throws on live token-exchange and permission paths — Every token-exchange request in a V2 realm now throws a 500 through `canExchangeTo`, and the client `management/permissions` endpoints fail the same way. Return false for exchange checks and a no-op for `setPermissionsEnabled` instead of throwing on live paths.

**Also found in:**
- `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:77-95`

Client permission listings return null display names — The CLIENTS type isn't handled in the name resolution, so `getDisplayName()` stays null and PolicyResourceService returns null displayNames for every client permission listing. Resolve the client UUID to a readable label for this type.

Passkey-only users bypass required password factor via configuredFor — `configuredFor` lets a passkey satisfy a required password factor, so possession-only passkeys replace the knowledge factor in step-up flows. Restrict the `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` shortcut to re-authentication or require a UV-checked passkey.

Passkeys widget missing from base login-password.ftl — Themes inheriting from `base`, including the legacy `keycloak` login theme, render no passkey UI because `base/login/login-password.ftl` lacks the macro. Add the `passkeys.ftl` import and `passkeys.conditionalUIData` call there too.

Organization clause in shared login predicate hides org-linked IDPs — `getLoginPredicate()` also backs `IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate()`, so this clause silently hides org-linked IDPs without `BROKER_PUBLIC=true` from the linked-federated-identity list when organizations are disabled. Move the organization clause into the cache layer's invalidation predicate, not the shared login predicate.

Login cache invalidation uses org-aware enabled state for original IDP — For an IDP bound to a disabled organization, `original.isEnabled()` is false even though the IDP sits in the login cache, so an update to `hideOnLogin` or `linkOnly` returns early and leaves stale entries. Test `getLoginPredicate()` on the stored model from `idpDelegate.getById(...)` instead of the wrapped `original`.

Login IDP cache key omits organizationId, causing unbounded entry growth — Keying the login cache by realm and `FetchMode` only lets each new `organizationId` grow the same `IdentityProviderListQuery` and evict the whole entry cluster-wide via `invalidateObject`, forcing DB reloads. Include `organizationId` in the key, as `cacheKeyOrgId` does for `getByOrganization`.

Feature-flagged table branch renders empty data, discarding result and fields — With `use-table-widget-visualization` enabled, the hardcoded empty `tableData` and `columns={[]}` discard `result.data`, `result.meta`, and the widget fields, so every table widget renders empty. Pass the real result and fields, or keep `StyledSimpleTableChart` until the migration is wired up.

Unbounded nodestore fan-out in replay breadcrumb summary error fetch — `fetch_error_details` loads every error id from nodestore per request, and `NodeStorage.get_multi` issues a backend read per id, so large replays cause unbounded fan-out. Bound the ids (e.g. the most recent N) or batch the lookup before building `node_ids`.

Error timestamps compared against replay-relative offsets — Comparing an absolute `ErrorEvent` `timestamp` against the replay-relative `event["timestamp"]` offset makes the merge test always true or always false, so errors flush as one block instead of interleaving. Normalize both to the same base before comparing.

Sleep patch makes flusher delay a no-op causing flaky test — The `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", ...)` patch also intercepts `time.sleep(0.1)`, so the delay never happens and `(msg,) = messages` can raise `ValueError`. Bind the real function with `from time import sleep`, as `test_flusher.py` does, or patch `time.sleep` only inside the flusher module.

Redis memory INFO fanout is repeated for every flusher buffer — Each flusher buffer repeats the identical cluster-wide `iter_cluster_memory_usage` fanout, so the summed `used`/`available` are N-times-duplicated cluster totals. Query the cluster memory once per `submit()` instead of iterating over every `self.buffers` entry.

wait_produce timer uses "shards" tag key while sibling metrics use "shard" — The `shards` tag key prevents the `wait_produce` timer from being correlated with the `produce` and `segment_size_bytes` timers that use `shard`. Use `tags={"shard": shard_tag}` to match.

queued default evaluated once at import, not per instance — Every `AssignmentSource` built during the worker's lifetime reports the same import-time timestamp, so `queued` cannot measure latency or distinguish two sources. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance records its own queue time.

sync_status_outbound's assignment_source is never passed by its only caller — The status path gets no source-based cycle prevention because the only caller in `tasks/sync_status_outbound.py` never forwards `assignment_source` or passes it to `should_sync`. Thread the source through the status task and `should_sync`, or drop the parameter from the abstract contract.

OAuth state uses pipeline signature instead of per-flow nonce — `pipeline.signature` is a constant md5 of the view class names, so it can't bind the callback to the browser that started the flow, leaving the login-CSRF open. Generate a per-flow nonce with `secrets.token_hex()`, bind it via `pipeline.bind_state`, and compare against `pipeline.fetch_state`.

OAuth token exchange omits redirect_uri and grant_type — The exchange omits `redirect_uri`, so it no longer matches the authorization request per RFC 6749 and relies on GitHub's registered callback; if `absolute_uri` differs there, users hit the generic failure page. Pass the same `redirect_uri` and `grant_type=authorization_code` into the exchange `data`.

GitHub install skips ownership check when Integration row is absent — When the webhook hasn't created the `Integration` yet, the `Integration.DoesNotExist` branch calls `next_step()` and `build_integration` without checking that the authenticated GitHub user owns the `installation_id`, letting an attacker link another account's installation. Resolve the installation's `sender` from the GitHub API, or require the webhook-created `Integration`, and run the comparison on both branches.

**Also found in:**
- `src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:481-482`

Missing sender metadata crashes GitHub installation pipeline — Pipeline-created integrations never get a `sender` key in `integration.metadata` (only `build_integration` sets it), so indexing `["sender"]["login"]` raises and returns a 500 instead of the failure page. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and treat a missing value as failed verification.

GitHub OAuth token and user-info errors cause 500 — `safe_urlopen` and `get_user_info` can raise (HTTP errors, connection errors, the 30s timeout) outside the guarded block, producing a 500 instead of the `github-integration-failed` page. Wrap both calls in try/except and return `error(...)` on failure.

Test dedupe builds expected occurrence with wrong group key and value — `IssueOccurrence.__eq__` only compares `id`, so this assertion passes even if `build_occurrence_and_event_data` generates a wrong fingerprint, hiding any group-key regression. Build the expected occurrence with `expected_result.group_key` and the actual value `10`.

Monitor context discards transformed config and returns raw schedule_type — The transform on `config` never reaches the payload, so the occurrence context keeps the raw `schedule_type`. Return `config` in the dict so the display value is used.
